items.title: graphify 0.9.94
items.text:
Nineteen community pull requests. A security pass on ingestion: a fetched URL with no hostname, with a malformed or zero port, or with embedded user:pass@ credentials is now rejected before the request leaves, on the first fetch and on every redirect, and a text capture no longer follows a dangling symlink out of the corpus. Extraction and resolution: a Maven POM contributes only its own dependencies, a JS/TS member call on an untyped receiver stops guessing a same-named method in the same file, a CommonJS require binding no longer shadows the class the required file exports, and Objective-C category node ids stay repo-relative instead of embedding the absolute checkout path. SQL gets its own pass: T-SQL bracketed names are unbracketed, a GO batch separator ends the statement, cross-file table stubs fold onto their real definition, and a procedure emits reads_from/writes_to edges. Plus a markdown bare method only links when its class is cited, the MCP node lookup refuses a substring near-miss instead of answering with an unrelated node, a cross-repo edge points at the call site, Objective-C calls resolve across a split header/impl, an incremental build stops re-queuing files an extractor declined by design, a quoted Codex hook command for install paths with spaces, an IPv6 bracketed-Host serve fix, and a complete, drift-guarded --platform list in --help. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

Fix: security validate_url rejects a fetched URL that has no hostname (http:///path), a non-numeric, out-of-range, or zero port, or embedded user:pass@ credentials, before the request is made and again on every redirect, so a malformed or credential-bearing URL is no longer fetched or persisted into the graph; a normal @ in a path or query and a valid high port still pass (#4643, #4644, #4645, thanks @cellrishi-code).

Fix: manifest a Maven pom.xml contributes only its own <dependencies> (including those under <profiles>), not the version pins under <dependencyManagement> or a build plugin's own <dependencies>, so a parent or BOM POM no longer emits dependency edges it only manages (#4596, thanks @jayhemnani9910).

Fix: js a member call on an untyped receiver (x.foo() where x has no known type) is deferred to receiver-typed resolution instead of binding to a same-named method elsewhere in the file, so a spurious self-loop or cross-call edge is no longer emitted; this.foo(), a typed receiver, and a locally instantiated receiver still resolve (#4598, #4605, thanks @ayushcodes10; reported by @SaschaAndresGrimm).

Fix: js a CommonJS const X = require('./m') binding no longer mints a module-scope node that shadows the class the required file exports, so new X() resolves to the required declaration; a real const x = factory() binding still keeps its node (#4621, #4634, thanks @lab1207; reported by @sub4biz).

Fix: extract an Objective-C category's class and method node ids stay repo-relative instead of embedding the absolute checkout path, so a category file like Foo+Cat.h yields portable ids that match across machines and merge cleanly; two same-named categories in different directories stay distinct (#4666, #4642, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik; reported by @xiongjianxu).

Fix: codex the generated Codex PreToolUse hook command quotes the graphify executable path, so an install under a path containing a space no longer builds a broken hook command, matching the existing Claude and Gemini hooks (#4662, thanks @supercell02).

Fix: serve an IPv6 HTTP bind accepts its own bracketed Host header ([::1]:port), so a server bound to an IPv6 loopback no longer refuses every request with a 421 (#4656, thanks @zydo).

Fix: ingest a text capture never writes through an existing entry: the free-path search uses lstat, so a name that is a dangling symlink is treated as occupied and the capture is diverted instead of following the link and writing outside the corpus (#4657, thanks @zydo).

Fix: cli graphify --help lists every accepted --platform value (it had omitted amp, copilot, kilo, kimi, and antigravity-windows); the list is derived from the same source as the install usage so the two cannot drift, with a guard test (#4655, thanks @zydo).

Fix: sql T-SQL bracketed identifiers ([dbo].[Orders]) are unbracketed so a name matches across styles, and a stored procedure's body emits reads_from/writes_to edges for the tables it reads and writes; aliases, variables, temp tables, strings, and comments never become targets (#4635, #4649, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @RuVl).

Fix: sql a GO batch separator (a client command, not a terminator) ends the statement, so a statement after a GO with no trailing ; parses on its own instead of merging into one malformed node; a GO inside a string, comment, or column name is left alone (#4651, #4652, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: sql a table referenced before its CREATE TABLE is seen folds onto the real definition instead of staying a separate stub, and a schema-qualified name binds correctly, while two genuinely different tables in different schemas (dbo.Orders vs sales.Orders) stay distinct and a SQL stub no longer binds to a same-named class in another language (#4653, #4654, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: markdown a bare method name in prose (for example redis where only Cache.redis exists) only links to the method when the owning class is cited in the same document, so a plain word is no longer turned into a false references edge; a qualified Class.method or Class::method mention still resolves (#4609, #4617, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @saad-siddique).

Fix: mcp the get_node and get_neighbors tools, and the explain command, refuse a substring-only near-miss with candidate suggestions instead of returning an unrelated node as the answer; an exact or prefix match still resolves (#3917, #4618, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @Alexandre-Aktisea).

Fix: cross-repo a cross-repo call edge points at the real call site rather than the caller's header declaration, so the edge's source_file and source_location name the line that makes the call (#4668, #4669, thanks @xiongjianxu).

Fix: extract an incremental build no longer re-queues, on every run, a code file an extractor declined by design (for example a virtual-workspace manifest); the file is marked ast_empty and left alone, while a genuinely failed or transiently empty extraction is still retried (#2543, #4672, thanks @xiongjianxu).

Fix: objc a member call resolves when a class is split across a header and an implementation in different directories, binding the selector to its single definition; two unrelated same-named classes that both define the selector stay ambiguous and get no edge (#4673, #4674, thanks @xiongjianxu).

items.title: v1.107.0
items.text:
Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53.

Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.107.0

Verify using the release tag (convenience):

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.107.0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.107.0

Expected output:

The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key

Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53.

Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.2

Verify using the release tag (convenience):

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.106.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.2

Expected output:

The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key

items.title: [261021] Browsers Worth Installing on Linux in 2026
items.text:
TLDR

Classic & Mainstream: Firefox sticks to the independent Gecko engine; Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Brave, Vivaldi, etc.) dominate with excellent web compatibility.

Emerging & Forks: Firefox forks like Zen focus on vertical tabs and new interactions; Ladybird attempts to build a rare, brand-new independent engine from scratch.

items.title: graphify 0.9.93
items.text:
Twenty-two community pull requests. Extraction: a reference to a Kotlin type alias, C# delegate, Swift macro, Dart typedef, Python module function or Rust sibling-module use now resolves to its real declaration instead of minting a sourceless stub; Metal/CUDA GPU qualifiers no longer mint god nodes; extern "C" headers route to the C++ extractor; an extensionless script with a versioned-interpreter shebang is classified; and Obsidian vault-relative wikilinks resolve. Plus a credential-redaction pass on rationale labels, a node-confidence fold, a truncated-reply label decode, a .graphifyrc BOM fix, a GraphML multigraph export fix, two-repo file disambiguation in explain and path, a PDF-read warning, no skill writes on --version/--help, two PR-tooling fixes (slashed default branch, legacy CI statuses), and a skill partly-read-file recovery so a long file a subagent only skimmed is retried on the next --update instead of silently kept half-read. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

Fix: Kotlin a typealias declaration is extracted, so a field or parameter typed as the alias resolves to it instead of minting a sourceless cross-file stub (#4553, #4557, thanks @rajatnagda45).

Fix: C# a delegate declaration is extracted, so references resolve to it instead of a sourceless stub; built-in Func<>/Action<> stay external (#4552, #4556, thanks @rajatnagda45).

Fix: Swift macro declarations are extracted and a freestanding #macro(...) call resolves to the declaration; an unknown or standard-library macro stays unresolved rather than minting a stub (#4551, #4555, thanks @rajatnagda45).

Fix: Rust a use rooted at a sibling mod (for example use item::Thing;) now reaches its declaration, while an external use serde::... still does not hijack a same-named local type (#4564, #4567, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @almothafar-maf).

Fix: build a node's drifted or legacy confidence is folded onto the enum the same way edges and hyperedges already are, so a node no longer reaches graph.json with an unnormalized confidence (#4529, #4531, thanks @rudycelekli; reported by @grazenN).

Fix: llm community labels salvaged from a truncated reply are JSON-decoded, so an escaped label (\", \n, \uXXXX, surrogate pairs) is no longer kept with literal backslash escapes (#4537, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: rcfile .graphifyrc is read as utf-8-sig, so a file saved with a UTF-8 BOM no longer drops its first key (#4538, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: Dart a typedef is extracted as a type alias on its own line, including the legacy typedef R name(args) form, instead of a bogus variable of type typedef; a field or parameter typed by the alias resolves to it rather than minting a sourceless typedef stub (#4582, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).

Fix: Python a module.func() call resolves to the module child named exactly func, even when a same-key sibling (for example a FuncSchema class beside a func_schema function) previously made the lookup ambiguous and dropped the edge; it never binds to a same-named child of an unrelated module (#4577, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).

Fix: C++ Metal and CUDA GPU address/execution-space qualifiers (kernel, device, constant, __global__, __device__, ...) in a .metal/.cu file no longer mint sourceless god nodes; the kernel function still extracts and a <<<...>>> launch still resolves (#4550, #4554, thanks @rajatnagda45).

Fix: extract a .h header containing extern "C" is routed to the C++ extractor, so a C-API header the C grammar rejects extracts its symbols instead of nothing (#4526, thanks @bekzodibragimov2004-design).

Fix: extract credential-shaped text (API keys, tokens, Bearer tokens, private-key headers, user:pass@ URLs) in a comment or docstring that becomes a rationale label is redacted before it reaches graph.json, the viz or exports; ordinary identifiers such as git SHAs and UUIDs are left intact (#4566, thanks @0xkaushik-ai).

Fix: export GraphML export of a graph loaded as a MultiGraph (a graph with parallel edges, after #4500) no longer crashes with an empty output; parallel edges are written with distinct keys and round-trip through read_graphml (#4536, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: prs the default branch is derived by stripping only the refs/remotes/origin/ prefix, so a branch name that contains a slash (for example release/2.x) is kept whole and PRs against it are no longer all dropped as wrong-base (#4534, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: prs CI classification now reads legacy commit-status StatusContext state in addition to check-run conclusions, so a PR whose only signal is an external status (Jenkins, CircleCI) is classified correctly, with a failing status taking precedence (#4533, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: detect an extensionless script whose shebang names a versioned interpreter (#!/usr/bin/env python3.11, #!/bin/bash5, ruby3.2, ...) is now classified to its language instead of being skipped (#4535, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: detect when a PDF cannot be read (corrupt, encrypted, or a missing optional dependency) graphify prints a one-time warning naming the file instead of silently returning empty text, so a failed read is distinguishable from a text-less PDF (#4527, thanks @rudycelekli; reported by @grazenN).

Fix: markdown an Obsidian [[wikilink]] whose target begins with one of the scan root's own folder names (a vault-relative path) now resolves to the real page instead of a ghost node, restoring intra-vault connectivity (#4559, thanks @bercedev; reported by @CryptoRMac4).

Fix: explain / path two same-path files from different repos in a merged graph are kept distinct: an ambiguous name names each repo and the retry hint points at the full node id, instead of conflating them as one file (#4512, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @kaka-in-home).

Fix: cli graphify --version and --help no longer rewrite or back up an installed skill file; only a real command refreshes skills (the staleness warning still prints) (#4545, thanks @bercedev; reported by @EmanuelFaria).

Fix: query a bare name that is the exact name of several nodes (for example a .nonce() method in two files) is refused with the candidates listed and the ambiguous exit code, matching explain and path; a keyword that only prefix- or substring-matches labels still runs a normal search (#4511, #4517, thanks @shivampal46011; reported by @kaka-in-home).

Fix: skill a long file a subagent only partly read is no longer a silent, permanent loss. On the skill extraction path each chunk now self-reports the lines it covered; a file whose reported coverage falls short of its real length is written to .graphify_partial.txt, cached as partial (which the loader treats as a miss) and left unstamped in the manifest, so the next --update re-dispatches it and replace-on-re-extract swaps the half-read node set for a complete one. This mirrors the library path's truncated-reply recovery (#933, #1950); the already-extracted nodes are kept, and a file no subagent reported is not falsely flagged (#3987, #2225, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @Ryanm218).

items.title: API reference pages in the editor, Admin MCP improvements, and more
items.text:
Breaking changes

Mintlify Index discontinued: The Index API returns 410 Gone and the Index MCP server tells connected agents to remove it. The dashboard no longer shows Index API keys, and the CLI no longer includes the mint index command.

Admin MCP tool changes: The admin MCP renames save to publish. Tools that edit content require a branch argument, and create_branch, discard, and status replace checkout, discard_session, and get_session_state. Dedicated project management tools replace the search_code_operations and execute_code code mode tools. Update prompts or scripts that call the old tools.

OpenAPI and API playground

OpenAPI 3.2: Mintlify accepts OpenAPI 3.2 documents. Tag hierarchies become nested navigation groups, and the API playground supports 3.2 additions such as the QUERY method and whole query string parameters. To upgrade a 3.1 document, change its openapi version.

Streaming responses: The API playground shows streaming responses as they arrive. Click Stop to end the request.

Editor and dashboard

API reference pages in the editor: Pages with openapi or api frontmatter show their endpoint and generated fields in the editor, so you can edit the content around them. See Pages.

Section links: Links to /page#heading open the page at that heading. Copy link to section in the block actions menu copies a dashboard link to the heading, and pasted section links show the section name.

Thumbnail settings: Set thumbnail overrides in page settings and in the settings for groups, tabs, and other navigation sections. See Edit page settings.

Unpublished site configuration: The site configuration view lists the sections with unpublished changes in a banner and marks them in the sidebar.

Print a page: Press Cmd + P to print the page content without the editor interface. See Keyboard shortcuts.

Agent mentions: Ask the agent to add teammate and page mentions to your content.

Haiku 5.5: Choose Haiku 5.5 in the agent's model picker.

Publishes: The Activity section of the dashboard is now Publishes, with Overview and Previews pages. See Deployments.

Admin MCP in the sidebar: Admin MCP settings and credentials have their own MCP item in the dashboard sidebar. Search MCP client credentials moved to the Docs MCP section of your project settings.

Regional translation targets: The Translate content automation can translate into British, Australian, and Canadian English and into Mexican and Latin American Spanish. See Manage automations.

Published sites

OG image presets: Choose a classic, headline, or minimal layout for generated OG images, with custom fonts, a brand or neutral background, and an eyebrow label above the title. Override the settings for individual pages and sections. See thumbnails.

Preview OG images: Run mint og to render a page's OG image to a PNG file.

Visibility by sign-in state and group: Show content only to signed-in readers, signed-out readers, or specific groups, and hide it from groups with excludes. See Visibility.

Regional language variants: navigation.languages accepts regional codes such as en-GB, es-MX, and es-419, and the language switcher shows the region. Language routing sends visitors to the variant that matches their browser. See Regional variants.

hreflang tags: Sites with multiple languages link each page to its translations with hreflang tags, so search engines can show readers the right language. See Alternate language links.

TypeDoc categories: SDK reference navigation follows the @category and @group tags in your TypeDoc artifact. See Generated pages.

Preview deployments: The robots.txt file on preview deployments disallows crawling.

Navigation on authenticated sites: Signed-out visitors on sites with authentication see the public navigation on first load, without layout shifts.

Server-rendered custom components: Custom components that you define with export and that only place their props into HTML render on the server, so they no longer pop in after the page loads. See React components.

AI and MCP

Admin MCP comment tools: The admin MCP can read comment threads, start a comment, suggest a tracked change, reply, and resolve threads. See Comments.

Merge from the admin MCP: Pass merge: true to publish to merge the branch's pull request when your project allows edits to the deploy branch. See Branches and publishing.

User ID on MCP events: Search tool calls through an authenticated MCP server record the signed-in user's sub claim as user_id in analytics streaming. Available on Enterprise plans.

Redacted assistant conversations: Email addresses and phone numbers in assistant conversations appear redacted in the dashboard, CSV exports, and the analytics API. Available on Pro and Enterprise plans.

Bug fixes

Editor: Footnotes render instead of showing a warning. Keyboard text selection works across tables. Comment cards stay anchored when you switch tabs, and block menu actions follow their block when content shifts. Autolinked URLs include their paths, queries, and sections and leave out trailing punctuation. Bare domains link to https://. The docs.json tab is titled Site settings.

Comments: The comment popover hides reply and actions when you can't comment. If your organization uses roles, admins can delete any comment or thread.

Published sites: Tabs no longer clip ordered list numbers from 10 up. Related pages pick the right language for index pages.

CLI: mint a11y checks files that use custom heading IDs. mint broken-links reports every page it can't parse instead of stopping at the first, no longer flags valid code inside <MDX> fragments, and resolves relative links in snippets.

Desktop app: Switching organizations no longer switches you back to the previous organization.

Multi-repo: Each GitHub source fetches content through its own installation.

Analytics API: Export date parameters accept ISO 8601 time zone offsets and fractional seconds.

Twenty-three community pull requests: call-resolution and id-collision fixes across JS/TS, Python, Go, Rust and Solidity; graph round-trip, dedup and confidence-folding fixes; skill code-only-update and dispatch fixes; and LLM/Ollama and detection fixes. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

Fix: JS/TS class members differing only by _, $ or # are kept as separate nodes (#4475, #4479, thanks @Mpasha17).

Fix: TypeScript this.field is typed from an assignment in any method, including static and accessors (#4473, #4482, thanks @FolatheDuckofDuckingburg).

Fix: JS a workspace package whose exports points only into dist/ falls back to src/ (#4485, #4489, thanks @bercedev).

Fix: JS a dangling barrel-named import edge is dropped once the import resolves through the barrel (#4486, #4488, thanks @bercedev).

Fix: Python module-level class ids colliding with a function or class are salted apart (#2810, #4467, thanks @hementhu).

Feature: Python a member call on a pytest fixture parameter is typed from the fixture's returned class (#4332, #4333, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).

Fix: Go / Rust same-file declarations differing only by case are kept as separate nodes (#4468, thanks @abdulsamie10).

Feature: Solidity inherited calls, super calls and modifiers resolve through C3 linearization (#4379, #4384, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).

Fix: MCP parallel edges are preserved through the graph.json round-trip and query output (#4500, #4503, thanks @rtmalikian).

Fix: dedup a node with a source_file beats a sourceless namesake in collision rank (#4492, #4496, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: build model-drifted string confidences fold to a valid value before validation and dedup (#4495, #4501, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: extractors the in-flight scan root is shared via the extractors base module, restoring the one-way import direction (#3666, #3758, thanks @abhay-codes07).

Fix: detect only a valid .git is treated as a VCS root, so a stray home-dir .git no longer leaks its .gitignore (#4444, #4464, thanks @Mpasha17).

Fix: hooks post-merge rebuilds on real merges, and a new post-rewrite hook rebuilds after cherry-pick/rebase/pull --rebase (#4463, #4476; #4490, #4491, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: skill the code-only --update path materializes the extraction before the merge across all hosts (#4447, #4313, thanks @vibhanshu-mishra; aider/devin #4456, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: skill stray backticks inside a double-quoted -c block no longer run a command mid-step (#4461, #4462, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: skill Pi dispatches semantic subagents to the native delegate agent (#4494, #4502, thanks @bercedev).

Fix: skill the agent pushes to the exact Neo4j/FalkorDB URI supplied, not a localhost example (#4349, thanks @vibhanshu-mishra).

Fix: llm the extraction prompt pins source_file to the dispatched file (#3377, #2270, #4487, thanks @cornwe19).

Feature: llm opt-in backend selection via GRAPHIFY_BACKEND, a disable switch, and an honest auto-detect (#4361, #4376, thanks @nothariharan).

Fix: deps cap tree-sitter-dm <0.26 so a fresh install cannot pull the ABI-incompatible 0.26 grammar (#4044, thanks @safishamsi).

items.text:
OAuth Proxy for non-DCR providers

Canary release (mcp-use@2.10.0-canary.4) adding an OAuth authorization server in front of identity providers without dynamic client registration, secret-free production builds, and .gitignore-aware deployments. Stable v2.10.0 has not shipped.

New (server): oauthProxy() in mcp-use/oauth makes the MCP server its own authorization server in front of GitHub (github()), Google (google()), or any OAuth 2.0 provider (upstream()). Clients present a client ID metadata document or register (DCR), approve a server-owned consent page that names the server by its host, and receive the proxy's own opaque tokens (#2822)

New (server): the clients option limits which clients may connect, by metadata document URL, origin, or a client defined on the server (#2822)

New (server): the upstream client secret and user tokens stay on the server, encrypted in a shared store from mcp-use/oauth/storage: Upstash, Redis, Postgres, Firestore, Cloudflare D1 or Durable Object, or in-memory for local development. redisStorage takes a connected client or a lazy connect function (#2822)

New (server): tools read the upstream token with upstreamToken(ctx.auth) or ctx.auth.upstream (#2822)

Enhancement (server): failed sign-ins and refreshes log the cause without token or code values (provider error code and description, HTTP status and content type, mismatched iss, or network error); refused client metadata documents and records encrypted with a retired secret are also logged (#2822)

Enhancement (server): clients that signed in through the 1.x oauthProxy keep working while registration is on; users approve the consent page once and sign in again without removing the server (#2822)

New (server): OAuth providers can register public HTTP routes from setup() with host.route(), read host.mode and host.listenHost, and compute oauthMetadata from the resolved resource URL (#2822)

Fix (server): OAuth endpoints under the MCP path are never written to trace logs, and oauthEnvironmentValue no longer throws on runtimes without process (#2822)

Fix (server): trailing-slash trimming in upstashStorage and the GitHub and Google upstream providers no longer uses a backtracking regex

New (server, @mcp-use/cli): mcp-use build evaluates the entry with MCP_USE_PHASE=build and no longer needs runtime secrets; the new isBuilding() export lets module-scope code skip reading secrets or connecting to a database. oauthProxy and upstashStorage require no secrets or credentials while building (#2830)

Fix (@mcp-use/cli): mcp-use build exits when the build finishes, even if the entry opened a connection at module scope such as a Redis client (#2830)

Fix (@mcp-use/cli): mcp-use build builds for production when NODE_ENV is unset. Views no longer ship React's development build, and server-side JSX no longer compiles to jsxDEV, which failed under mcp-use start (#2830)

Fix (@mcp-use/cli): a failed build or dev start prints the cause of a refused connection instead of an empty line (#2830)

New (@mcp-use/cli): mcp-use deploy --no-github applies .gitignore rules when packaging, including wildcards, directory rules, and negation, while keeping the baseline cloud exclusions (#2485)

Fix (server): MCPServer.fromOpenAPI converts OpenAPI 3.0 boolean exclusiveMinimum and exclusiveMaximum into JSON Schema numeric bounds instead of throwing while registering tools (#2717)

Fix (@mcp-use/agent): the Anthropic provider sends "[no content]" for empty tool result content, avoiding HTTP 400 errors from the Messages API (#2693)

0.9.90 (2026-10-13)

Fourteen community pull requests: C# call-resolution and id-collision fixes, Python/Go/dedup correctness, a hub-label sidecar, a post-merge heal hook, and query/build fixes. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

Fix: C# a nameless member-call receiver (run.Sequence.Apply(), Make().Apply()) no longer mis-binds to the caller's own same-named method; every C# member call defers and resolves only through a typed receiver (#4422, thanks @nixvideojuego-ui).

Fix: C# new X() no longer binds to a method that shares the type's name, same-file or cross-file; a real same-named type still wins (#4428, thanks @nixvideojuego-ui).

Feature: C# foreach loop variables are now typed from the collection's element type (arrays, known sequences, dictionary .Keys/.Values), so calls on the loop variable resolve; untypable iterables stay unresolved (#4423, thanks @nixvideojuego-ui).

Fix: C# node ids now keep names that differ only by a leading/trailing _ or by case apart (Action/_Action, Load/load, Token/TOKEN), in both ids and member-call resolution keys, instead of collapsing one onto the other (#4415, #4416, thanks @JensD-git).

Fix: C# colliding ids are salted before the partial-class merge, so a partial half keeps its members and an unrelated node sharing a half's id is no longer deleted (#4411, #4412, thanks @JensD-git).

Fix: Go a generic receiver type (func (b *Box[T]) ...) is normalized before building its id, so a generic type's methods attach to the type node instead of a separate Box[T] node (#4438, thanks @Goodkamalpandey).

Fix: Python a module member call (mod.func()) now resolves when the caller is a method or nested function, by walking the enclosing scopes to the file node instead of reading only the immediate parent (#2447, #4437, thanks @SrijanSriv).

Fix: an edge between two surviving nodes is no longer dropped just because its own source_file was not dispatched this run; it is kept as long as both endpoints are kept nodes (#2276, #4436, thanks @SrijanSriv).

Fix: dedup keeps a dropped-folder document next to a top-level file that mints the same id (protocol.md beside docs/protocol.md and docs/firmware/protocol.md), path-qualifying the siblings instead of collapsing and losing one; a genuine reference still collapses onto the named file (#4281, #4410, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: Jinja templates (.j2, .jinja, .jinja2) are now classified as documents instead of being dropped from the graph (#3427, #3455, thanks @nikhilsaxena04).

Fix: build source-less placeholder nodes orphaned by a re-extraction that drops their edges are now swept on a normal (non-prune) incremental build, not just under prune; the sweep removes only code placeholders and external stubs and spares disk-isolated, fresh-isolated, and hyperedge-member nodes (#4399, thanks @Mpasha17).

Fix: query the fallback traversal now retains relationships among the visited nodes (seed-to-seed edges, cycles, cross-links, and parallel relations), via the induced subgraph, instead of printing only tree edges (#4314, #4315, thanks @vibhanshu-mishra).

Feature: watch hub-fallback community labels now go to a .graphify_labels.pending.json sidecar, so the tracked .graphify_labels.json holds only curated (manual/LLM) names; a promoted name drops from the sidecar and an emptied sidecar is removed (#3334, #3551, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Feature: hooks graphify hook install now also installs a post-merge hook that runs an unscoped background rebuild after a merge, healing a symbol the graph.json union merge driver resurrected on one side (which nothing else would re-extract), so the phantom node no longer persists (#2418, #3556, thanks @ayushcodes10).

items.text:
0.9.89 (2026-10-13)

Sixteen community pull requests: cross-repo member-call resolution (Go, PHP, TypeScript, Kotlin, Objective-C), generic/template type-parameter cleanup (Kotlin, Scala, C++, Swift), an Objective-C enum extractor, interface-dispatch fan-out, a native Pi guard extension, and several resolution/ingest fixes. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

Feature: cross-repo member calls now finish across a repository boundary for Go, PHP, TypeScript/JS, Kotlin and Objective-C: a call whose receiver type is declared in another repo is parked by name during the single-repo build and bound on merge-graphs/global add against a unique same-named exported type, fail-closed on ambiguity (#3152, #3388, #3393, #3385, #3387, #3389, #3391, #3395, thanks @xiongjianxu).

Fix: Go a package's type whose methods span several files now folds into one node instead of fragmenting under _disambiguate_colliding_node_ids, so single-definition guards and receiver typing work (#3399, #3400, thanks @xiongjianxu).

Fix: Kotlin / Scala / C++ / Swift generic and template type parameters (class Box<T>, [T], template<typename T>, struct Stack<Element>) no longer mint sourceless stub god-nodes; a real same-named type is still referenced (#4406, #4407, #4408, #4409, thanks @rajatnagda45).

Feature: Objective-C NS_ENUM and NS_OPTIONS declarations are now extracted as an enum type plus its members, with the macro forms validated and malformed macros rejected fail-closed (#4400, #4401, thanks @oleksii-tumanov).

Feature: dispatch an interface member now links to every implementer, not just one, so a DI chain through a multi-implementer interface resolves; the fan-out is gated to genuine implementers with a correct method match (#3800, #4396, thanks @Goodkamalpandey).

Feature: Pi a native Pi guard extension now runs graphify hook-guard before Pi's tool calls and also loads under Oh My Pi, so the hook-guard policy reaches Pi; install/uninstall delegates to pi install/pi remove and the guard fails open (#4378, thanks @andrebrait).

Feature: hook a firing read/search nudge now shows the graph nodes behind the nudged call and tightens its wording, so agents act on it instead of treating it as noise; the graph read piggybacks on the already-bounded nudge and is injection-safe and size-capped (#4368, thanks @andrebrait).

Fix: resolution a .js import now resolves to a .tsx source when no real .js file exists, matching TypeScript's NodeNext resolution; a real .js still wins (#3486, #4395, thanks @DevChiniwala).

Fix: distinct downloaded binary captures (PDFs/images) whose URLs collide to one filename are now kept under numbered names instead of silently overwriting each other, matching the markdown path's de-dup (#4393, #4394, thanks @oleksii-tumanov).

items.title: v0.9.88
items.text:
0.9.88 (2026-10-12)

Twenty community pull requests: language-extraction and call-resolution fixes (Java, C/C++, Python, Swift, Go, PowerShell, C#, JS/EJS), dedup/shrink-guard hardening, and query/graph.html ergonomics. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

Feature: Java a call on a chained, new or cast receiver (factory.builder().size(3).build(), new Builder().size(1), ((Builder) o).build()) now resolves through the declared return types on the method chain, binding only on a single unambiguous target (#4306, #4307, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).

Fix: Java a bare call or field receiver inherited from a supertype in another file now resolves to the nearest declaring supertype (class wins over an interface default; a tie binds nothing), instead of dangling (#4304, #4305, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).

Fix: C/C++ a quoted cross-directory include (#include "../lib/foo.h", STM32 Core/Src to Core/Inc) now resolves to the right header by a unique longest-shared-directory-prefix match, fail-closed on ties and never guessing for ./, ../, absolute or angle-bracket includes (#4354, #4392, thanks @hopstreax).

Fix: Python a @name.setter/.getter/.deleter decorator no longer mints a sourceless stub node (#4380, #4385, thanks @rajatnagda45).

Fix: Python a Self (PEP 673) type annotation (-> Self, : Self, typing.Self) no longer mints a sourceless self stub (#4381, #4386, thanks @rajatnagda45).

Fix: Swift a Self type annotation no longer mints a sourceless self stub (#4382, #4387, thanks @rajatnagda45).

Fix: Go generic type parameters ([T any]) in signatures, struct fields and interface methods no longer mint sourceless t/r stubs (#4383, #4388, thanks @rajatnagda45).

Fix: Python a class type-hinted before it is defined (a forward reference) no longer mints a bare stub that collides with and swallows the file node (#4334, #4343, thanks @Mpasha17).

Fix: C# extraction now recovers members declared after a verbatim interpolated string that ends in an escaped quote ($@"a""{e}"""), instead of silently dropping the rest of the file; the fix masks only the offending bytes and discards the rewrite unless it re-parses clean (#3376, #3612, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).

Fix: PowerShell dot-sourced includes with quoted or $PSScriptRoot paths now emit import edges, and script-scope commands (outside any function) are now collected as calls (#4356, #4369, thanks @FabioRueda).

Fix: JS/TS a bare or scoped external import is now anchored to the package name rather than the path leaf, so @scope-a/utils and @scope-b/utils stay distinct and lodash/fp/map collapses onto one lodash node (#3084, #3092, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).

Feature: EJS (.ejs) templates now have an extractor: scriptlet functions/classes, require/import edges, dynamic imports, and <%- include('partial') %> composition edges, instead of a single top-level parse error (#3811, #4338, thanks @nothariharan).

Fix: serve a dotted Python query (pkg.mod.func, pkg.mod:func) now resolves to the symbol by module path, fail-closed on a same-file ambiguity, without regressing bare-name lookups (#4366, #4367, thanks @Mpasha17).

Fix: dedup now path-qualifies semantic ids that dropped the directory, so a/x.md and b/x.md (both minting a bare x) stay distinct instead of collapsing and losing one node; a reference to the bare id from a third file is left unresolved with a warning rather than guessed (#4281, #4362, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: a semantic node that dedup legitimately folded into its AST twin is now exempt from the shrink guard, so graphify update on a graph that had an LLM semantic ghost is no longer wrongly write-blocked; the exemption is scoped to a strict _origin=="ast" twin at the same path and label, so a genuine partial-build loss is still refused. LLM node/edge field aliases (file/filepath, relationship) are folded, with the canonical field always winning (#4389, #4391, thanks @AndresDiagoM).

Fix: install graphify install/uninstall now removes only graphify's own hook entries (keyed on the hook-guard/hook-check command, not a loose "graphify" substring), keeping co-located user hooks and other commands in the same group, and routes uninstall through a backup (#4359, #4373, thanks @nothariharan).

Fix: install CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and sibling files now keep their original line endings (CRLF or LF) across install and uninstall, instead of being normalized to the platform default (#4360, #4372, thanks @nothariharan).

Fix: wiki index rows now link to their own article when two communities or god-nodes share a label, instead of both pointing at the first-registered slug and orphaning the second article (#3032, #3033, #3095, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).

Feature: query --seed starts the traversal at given nodes (ids, labels, callable names or paths) so an external ranker can choose the start set; unresolved seeds are reported and skipped, and an all-unresolved set fails closed rather than falling back to keyword seeds (#4293, #4289, thanks @devkancheti4-design).

Feature: graph.html the sidebar now shows a hover tooltip with the full (truncated) legend/search/neighbor name and the legend node count; user text is written via textContent, preserving the embedded-JSON escaping (#4286, #4291, thanks @Hassannzidan).

items.title: v0.9.87
items.text:
0.9.87 (2026-10-12)

Eighteen community pull requests: language-extraction fixes (PHP, C#, Python, TypeScript, Julia), retrieval and watch hardening, and skill/benchmark correctness.

Fix: PHP a Class::method() static call now resolves to the called method rather than binding to the class node, and no longer stalls at INFERRED confidence for a same-namespace call that needs no use import. self/static/parent and lowercase class receivers route through the PHP resolver, fail-closed on any ambiguous or off-corpus receiver (#3872, #3874, thanks @rikurunico).

Fix: C# nested and generic partial types now merge by their full type path (Outer\1.Inner), so a two-file nested partial is unified while FooandFoo` stay distinct; a cross-file unqualified call binds to the caller's own merged type when it is the single own-type candidate, and a sourceless placeholder base is dropped when a real same-named base exists on the partial (#4363, #4364, thanks @JensD-git). (The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.)

Feature: Python a read of a @property (obj.prop, including x.prop += v) now links to the property's getter, instead of being dropped as a bare attribute access (#4337, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky). (The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.)

Fix: TypeScript a public call c.name() reaches a #name-labeled node only when the class declares a public name, and a public call keeps its edge when foo and #foo share one node (#4298, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).

Fix: Julia parametric and module-qualified functor (callable-struct) types are named by their type rather than the variable, and never fall back to the variable binding (#4351, thanks @ayarodionov).

Fix: C# a var is typed from the called method's return type, so downstream member calls on it resolve (#4266, #4268, thanks @Mpasha17).

Fix: graphify affected <PR> now scopes graph impact to the requested PR instead of the repository default branch, and PR default-branch detection is isolated under test (#3829, thanks @hopstreax).

Fix: update refuses to drop a saved semantic node id when the node total grows (treating it as an incomplete re-extract), while still letting a removed import stub go; export keeps an integer node id that is still in the graph (#4115, thanks @SrijanSriv).

Fix: the MCP query_graph seed order no longer lets a weak match on an early-alphabet term lead a specific term's exact match: the per-term guaranteed seeds (#1445) are ordered by match strength (#4357, #4358, thanks @devkancheti4-design).

Fix: the update skill stamps _origin on the semantic tier so an AST-only update cannot delete semantic nodes it did not re-extract (#2843, #3110, thanks @abhay-codes07).

Feature: a project can declare what an ambiguous extension (.inc, .h, TS-family) means via language.<ext>=<language|.ext> lines in .graphifyrc; the declaration flows through classification, extractor selection, imports, watch, and the AST cache, and default detection is byte-for-byte unchanged when absent (#2961, #3789, thanks @andrebrait and @abhay-codes07).

Fix: the hook's soft read/search nudge is bounded per session instead of firing on every matching file (#3435, #3443, thanks @L4XB).

Fix: the update skill prints a short summary of the incremental step and leaves the full result in .graphify_incremental.json, instead of dumping every file path into the agent context (#3952, thanks @mdshzb04).

Fix: skillgen Step 3 Part A now passes root= to extract(), so adapting the snippet to a relocated cache (--out) no longer renames every code node and blinds the node-count shrink guard (#3727, #3955, thanks @jnrod03-rgb).

Fix: watch a full-corpus rebuild is no longer silently dropped when the rebuild lock is busy; it is queued (superseding queued incremental paths) and drained after the in-flight rebuild, and the "changes queued" log only prints when something was actually queued (#4274, #4276, thanks @smngvlkz).

Fix: the benchmark now counts the tokens of the answer query_graph actually returns (calling the real budgeted query path) instead of a separate unbudgeted reimplementation (#4347, #4348, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).

Feature: graph.html gains a light/dark/system theme toggle; the dark default renders byte-identically to before (#3894, #4300, thanks @Mpasha17).

Fix: labeling now honors the Claude CLI model environment variable (GRAPHIFY_CLAUDE_CLI_MODEL), matching the extraction path, so labeling no longer silently falls back to the session default model (#3846, #3876, thanks @oleksii-tumanov).

items.text:
Eighteen community pull requests: language-extraction fixes, safety and determinism hardening, and CLI/query ergonomics.

Safety: graphify uninstall --purge now refuses to delete the project (or home, or a filesystem root) when GRAPHIFY_OUT is empty or ., instead of silently removing the working tree (#4329, thanks @Hassannzidan).

Fix: Julia now extracts return-typed, qualified (Base.show), operator (Base.:+) and functor (callable-struct) methods, and resolves broadcast (f.(xs)) and pipe (x |> f) calls (#4310, thanks @ayarodionov).

Fix: Rust grouped use declarations (use a::{b, c::d}) now expand into one import binding per name, instead of a single edge to the common prefix (#4135, thanks @krishhgg). (The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.)

Fix: Scala 3 class Foo derives Bar now links the class to each derived typeclass (#2048, #4173, thanks @Mpasha17).

Fix: Codex semantic chunks are no longer clobbered by the shared B3 merge (each chunk is written to its own file, matching the other hosts), so semantic nodes/edges survive (#4311, #4312, thanks @vibhanshu-mishra).

Fix: affected <Symbol> now also walks callers of the supertype member that an overriding method overrides, so a change to an override surfaces users of the base contract (#4330, #4331, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).

Fix: dedup keeps combining marks in label normalization, so distinct Indic-script words no longer collapse to one node (#4317, #4318, thanks @Suraj370).

Fix: dedup ranks a relative source_file against the scan root rather than the CWD, so building from a subdirectory no longer strands an extension-renamed node's edges on the survivor (#4281, #4326, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: the global (cross-repo) graph preserves stored edge direction on global add, so path and other direction-aware readers no longer follow reversed arcs (#4066, #4138, thanks @e4c5).

Fix: graphify now respects git's global ignore file (core.excludesFile), with git-faithful precedence and ~/XDG expansion (#4335, #4339, thanks @smngvlkz).

Fix: null token counts from a backend are coerced to 0 across all backends, instead of crashing a chunk with a TypeError (#4325, #4340, thanks @rtmalikian).

Feature: built-in Ollama requests accept a sampling seed for reproducible extraction (#4168, thanks @oleksii-tumanov).

Fix: explain refuses a name carried by several nodes of one file (ambiguous within a file) instead of silently picking one (#4320, thanks @alexwrite).

Fix: lookups now return distinct exit codes — 0 for an answer, 3 for an ambiguous name, 4 for a missing one — so scripts can tell a miss from a hit (#4321, thanks @alexwrite).

Fix: explain/query tell you how to get the full answer (and add explain --all) when the output is truncated to the token budget (#4323, thanks @alexwrite).

Change: a committed graph.json is now written as one line of compact JSON, so re-running a build produces a +1/-1 diff instead of a large whitespace churn (#3413, #4319, thanks @andrebrait).

Docs: the always-on guidance explains that large graph.json diffs in pull requests are expected (#4324, thanks @andrebrait), and the README distinguishes local CLI skill guidance from MCP instructions (#3925, #4292, thanks @Tivonsico).

v4.1.0: Fourth and One

FastMCP 4.1.0 is a maintenance release at heart: a broad sweep of fixes across OpenAPI, proxies, auth, tasks, and the CLI, plus full Python 3.15 support. It doesn't change how most servers behave. A few security fixes do tighten inputs that FastMCP previously accepted, though, and our versioning policy keeps breaking changes out of patch releases, so this ships as a point-one release.

Check these before upgrading:

MultiAuth now qualifies client IDs by source, so existing MultiAuth sessions and tasks start new ownership scopes. Finish pending tasks before upgrading.

Regex tool search uses Pydantic's regex engine, which doesn't support lookarounds or backreferences.

Skill files must resolve inside their configured directories.

OpenAPI path parameters reject . and .. segments.

HTTP sessions now expire after the MCP SDK's 30-minute idle default instead of never.

CodeMode requires Monty 1.1, which renames max_duration_secs to max_feed_duration_secs.

Thanks to our 48 contributors, including 21 first-time contributors!

items.text:
Desktop app

Deep links: mintlify:// links open in the desktop app as a new tab.

Zoom and new tabs: Zoom in, zoom out, or reset the zoom from the View menu. Cmd + N opens a new tab with a blank page.

Offline screen: Navigation changes you made while offline save when your connection returns. The app shows an offline screen if you lose your connection.

Find in page: Press Cmd + F to search the current page. See Keyboard shortcuts for more information.

Check for updates: Check for a new version from the app menu or settings. See Updates for more information.

Browser sign-in: Sign in to the desktop app through your default browser. If browser sign-in isn't available for your organization, sign in inside the app. See Sign in for more information.

Agent and AI

Agent replies to comments: The agent can read open comments and suggestions on a page, reply to threads, and resolve comment threads.

Google Docs integration: Connect Google Docs as a read-only personal integration so the agent can search and read your documents. Available on Enterprise plans.

Admin MCP: The admin MCP can edit your deploy branch directly when the branch doesn't require pull requests. It can also upload images and returns links to private pages. The diff shows who made each pending change.

Group-scoped MCP credentials: Assign user groups to MCP client credentials so they can access pages restricted to those groups. You can't change a credential's groups after you create it.

Custom skills on authenticated sites: Skills marked public: true appear for visitors who aren't signed in. See Share skills on authenticated sites.

Multiple pull requests per automation run: Custom automations can open several pull requests in one run, or add commits to a pull request that an earlier run opened. See Open multiple pull requests or append to open ones.

Tables and lists: HTML tables no longer lose rows on save, ordered lists in table cells keep their starting number, and task lists written with [X] no longer fail MDX validation.

Fixed credits for assistant answers: Each assistant answer uses 25 credits.

OpenAPI Overlays

Transform a spec: Use OpenAPI Overlays to rename paths, replace server URLs, or remove internal endpoints without editing the specification file. Overlays apply after a specification is parsed and before it is validated, so generated endpoint pages, navigation, openapi frontmatter, and mint validate all use the transformed document. See Transform your spec with overlays.

Overlay Specification 1.0 and 1.1: Write update, remove, and copy actions that select nodes with RFC 9535 JSONPath expressions. See Create an overlay document.

Reference or auto-discover overlays: Add an overlays property anywhere your docs.json accepts openapi, using a relative path or a URL. Or skip the configuration: an overlay with an extends field pointing at your specification is discovered automatically. See Auto-discover overlays.

items.text:
Notification preferences

Notification preferences: Choose which emails you receive for each event, including comment replies and mentions, thread resolutions, suggestions submitted, accepted, or rejected, automation runs, and product feedback. Configure preferences on the Notifications page of your dashboard.

Automation failure emails: Turn on automation run notifications to get an email when a run fails. Mintlify then holds further failure emails until a run succeeds again.

Share notifications: Mintlify notifies you when someone shares a page with you.

Editor and collaboration

Collaborative source mode: Source mode now supports real-time collaboration. See your teammates' cursors as they work on the same branch as you. Frontmatter edits sync live across visual and source mode. See Real-time editing.

Comment reactions: React to a comment with an emoji to acknowledge it without replying. Hover over a reaction to see who reacted, and reacting to someone else's comment notifies its author. See Comments.

Selective publish: Select individual changes in the publish menu to publish part of your pending work instead of everything at once.

Media on private pages: Upload images and videos to private pages. Private media is served only to people who can open the page, and it is removed when the page is deleted.

Editor polish: Search results show page titles and reveal the file in the sidebar, the sidebar lists only Markdown pages by default, the share dialog searches recipients by email address, the emoji suggestion menu has better search relevance, and the agent panel stays available in site settings.

Automations

Run scope for manual runs: When you trigger an automation manually, choose whether it reviews changes since a date, the entire site, or a specific pull request. See Run an automation manually.

Analytics

Page filter: Filter your analytics to a specific page with the new page dropdown in the dashboard.

API playground

Optional field toggles: In the playground modal, required fields sort first and optional fields collapse behind an Expand N optional fields control, with a global toggle in the header. Collapsed fields stay findable. Searching the page for a hidden field name expands the section that contains it, and values you entered persist across collapse and expand.

Collapse fields by default: Set expand: false under x-mint: playground on an operation to collapse nested object fields by default. See Collapse playground fields.

Authoring

mint test: Generate tests for the code blocks in your docs from the CLI. Runs are saved so you can revisit past reports. See mint test.

<MDX> improvements: Headings inside <MDX> blocks merge into the page's table of contents, ## Title {#id} anchors work at any indent, and code blocks inside <MDX> behave like code blocks at the page root. See MDX.

Markdown in component titles: Component titles, such as accordion titles, support inline Markdown formatting like code and bold.

Table column widths: HTML tables honor the <colgroup> widths you author.

Referrals

Enterprise referrals: Enterprise organizations can now participate in the referral program.

Bug fixes

Static exports: Static builds bundle your logo files so exported sites no longer reference missing assets.

GitLab subgroups: Repositories in nested GitLab subgroups sync correctly.

Large repositories: Repositories large enough that GitHub truncates their file listing now sync all files.

Assistant citations: Citations that dropped a leading path segment now open the correct page.

Authenticated previews: Preview deployments for docs behind authentication serve your changed files.

Translations: The translation automation writes locale-prefixed internal links, so newly translated pages link within their own language.

OpenAPI cleanup: Deleting an OpenAPI spec removes its generated assets from your site.

Custom fonts: Bold text stays bold when you set a custom body font weight.

Code feedback: The code snippet feedback popover displays above the table of contents panel.

Dismissed banners: Dismissed banners no longer flash on page load.

Editor fixes: Reference-style links and Link components render correctly, HTML tables with colspan or classes round-trip without changes, editing a page no longer reformats untouched content, and branch switching no longer causes redirect loops.

Refer a team to Mintlify from the Referrals page in your dashboard. When someone you refer starts a Pro plan, both of your organizations receive 50,000 credits. You can earn referral credits for up to three referrals. Available on Pro plans.

Authoring

<MDX> component: Wrap content in <MDX> to render Markdown formatting inside JSX expressions, such as conditional content. See MDX.

Custom styles on components: Built-in components now accept a className prop, and dynamic Tailwind utilities work inside it.

Editor and collaboration

Private page search: Editor search now includes your private pages, and you can open results directly from the search palette. See Private pages.

Agent replies to mentions: Mention @mintlify in a comment, suggestion, or reply and the editor agent answers in the same thread, including on private pages. See Ask the Mintlify agent.

Clickable agent questions: When the editor agent asks a clarifying question, click an option to answer instead of typing.

SVG attachments: Attach SVG files to editor agent messages. See Attach files.

Faster branching: Creating a branch in the editor switches you to it instantly and the editor now guides you through branch protection rules.

Editor polish: Math expressions update their rendered preview live as you type, the component properties panel has a refreshed design and autosaves your changes, and opening an editor link that belongs to another of your organizations prompts you to switch instead of showing an error.

Automations

Redesigned automation runs: The runs tab shows a grouped feed of each run's results, including pull requests, modified pages, and failures, with status filters and a review-needed indicator. See Manage automations.

Analytics

mint analytics: View traffic stats, search queries, feedback, and assistant conversations from the CLI. See mint analytics.

Docs and agents

Discoverable llms.txt indexes: The root llms.txt now links to the per-section indexes under /_llms, and optional links are indexed by navigation scope. See llms.txt.

Index MCP rate limit: The daily rate limit for the Mintlify Index MCP server is raised to 5,000 requests. See Index MCP reference.

Publishing permissions for AI apps: Changing whether your MCP server pushes directly to your deploy branch now requires an admin role. Editors see the setting as read-only.

Bug fixes

Safari media: Images and videos now load correctly in Safari.

Accordions: HTML tables inside accordions render instead of being dropped.

Code groups: Expandable code blocks inside a CodeGroup no longer grow past their collapsed height.

iOS zoom: Focusing search and assistant inputs on iOS no longer zooms the page.

Favicons: Favicon URLs resolve correctly on deployments with a custom base path.

API playground: Enum array items render their values instead of type labels.

llms.txt languages: Language-specific llms.txt routes are scoped to their language, the default language is prioritized, and llms-full.txt headings and links are normalized.

mint format: CLI formatting now matches the editor's output, so formatting a file no longer produces spurious diffs.

Editor fixes: Removing a page icon persists, focus returns to the page after toolbar dropdown picks, and deleting the page you have open redirects instead of showing a stale view.

Assistant widget: The widget refreshes its configuration before it expires, so long-lived pages keep a working assistant.

Since then, the community has filed five independent Specification Enhancement Proposals (SEPs) proposing new annotations, driven in part by a sharper collective understanding of where risk actually lives in agentic workflows. items.title: LM Studio 0.3.23 — Reasoning content and tool‑calling reliability
items.text: For gpt‑oss on POST /v1/chat/completions , reasoning content moves out of message.content and into choices.message.reasoning (non‑streaming) and choices.delta.reasoning (streaming), aligning with o3‑mini ‡ . Tool names are normalized (e.g., snake_case) before being provided to the model to improve tool‑calling reliability ‡ . Fixed errors for certain tools‑containing requests to POST /v1/chat/completions (e.g., "reading 'properties'") and non‑streaming tool‑call failures ‡ .

items.title: LM Studio 0.3.19 — Bug fixes for streaming and tool calls
items.text: Corrected usage statistics returned by OpenAI‑compatible streaming responses ‡ . Improved handling of parallel tool calls via the streaming API ‡ . Fixed parsing of correct tool calls for certain Mistral models ‡ .

items.title: LM Studio 0.3.18 — Streaming options and tool‑calling improvements
items.text: Added support for the stream_options object on OpenAI‑compatible endpoints. Setting stream_options.include_usage to true returns prompt and completion token usage during streaming ‡ . Errors returned from streaming endpoints now follow the correct format expected by OpenAI clients ‡ . Tool‑calling support added for Mistral v13 tokenizer models, using proper chat templates ‡ . The response_format.type field now accepts "text" in chat‑completion requests ‡ . Fixed bugs where parallel tool calls split across multiple chunks were dropped and where root‑level $defs in tool definitions were stripped ‡ .

items.title: LM Studio 0.3.17 — Tool‑calling reliability and token‑count updates
items.text: Token counts now include the system prompt and tool definitions ‡ . This makes usage reporting more accurate for both the UI and the API. Tool‑call argument tokens are streamed as they are generated ‡ , improving responsiveness when using streamed function calls. Various fixes improve MCP and tool‑calling reliability, including correct handling of tools that omit a parameters object and preventing hangs when an MCP server reloads ‡ .
